spec.title: Evidence from behind an endpoint
spec.intro:
The truth of the control "every workforce user has MFA enabled" no longer sits in a
file you can ls — it sits behind a vendor's API. Your job: walk up to the counter,
prove who you are, pull EVERY page of the answer, compute the metric, and keep
evidence an auditor can re-run. This terminal is the lab's Linux box with one
addition: curl is wired to the (fictional) vendor acme.example — its responses are
the lab's committed fixture bytes and its documented error shapes, never invented.
The vendor's API documentation is on the box as ~/lab06/vendor-docs.md. Two honest
boundaries: bun and git are not installed here (exactly as the pinned lab container
lacks them), so the module's aggregator runs as its PATH port `aggregate-mfa` —
byte-locked to the real `bun aggregate-mfa.ts` output — and the §6 Git step happens
on your real machine. The lab folder arrives exactly as `bash labs/setup.sh` writes it.

tasks.instruction:
LOCATE starts with the docs, not with code. Move into the lab (`cd lab06`),
look around (`ls`, `ls fixtures`), and read the vendor's API reference
(`cat vendor-docs.md`). Find the five answers §4.7 says you need: auth rung,
endpoint + truth field, pagination + stop signal, rate limit, error shape.

hints.nudge: Reading an unfamiliar vendor's docs and answering five questions fast IS the durable skill — the code is mechanics.

hints.concept: §4.7 — reading vendor API docs is the actual skill

hints.reveal: cd lab06, then: ls · ls fixtures · cat vendor-docs.md

tasks.explain:
You now know everything the pull needs before writing a line of it: OAuth2
client-credentials at /oauth/token, GET /api/v2/users with `mfa_enabled` as the
truth field, cursor pagination stopping at null, 600 req/min, and the
{error, message} error shape. That five-line understanding IS the LOCATE stage.

tasks.instruction:
Knock on the counter with no credentials and read the verdict BEFORE the payload:
`curl -i acme.example/api/v2/users > unauth-response.txt`, then `cat` the file.
The status line is the clerk's answer; the body explains it.

hints.nudge: `-i` makes curl print the status line and headers above the body — the verdict before the payload. `>` keeps what came back as evidence.

hints.concept: §4.2 — status codes are the verdict; read them before the payload

hints.reveal: curl -i acme.example/api/v2/users > unauth-response.txt, then: cat unauth-response.txt

tasks.explain:
401 means "who are you?" — an authentication problem. The script that parses
this body as if it were users would happily report zero users without MFA.
Reading the status first is the single cheapest bug-prevention habit in
evidence collection.

tasks.instruction:
Climb the right rung: exchange the lab's client credentials (they're in
vendor-docs.md) for a short-lived bearer token, requesting ONLY the scope this
control needs (`users:read`). Save the response as `token.json` and `cat` it —
you'll need the access_token for every call that follows.

hints.nudge: POST the form fields grant_type, client_id, client_secret, and scope to the token endpoint. curl's `-d` sends a form body (and makes the request a POST).

hints.concept: §4.3 — the authentication ladder: client-credentials trades a storable secret for an ephemeral token

hints.reveal: curl -s -d 'grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=grc_evidence_bot&client_secret=cs_4d2b9e7f1a8c6053b4e2d9f7c1a08e35&scope=users:read' acme.example/oauth/token > token.json, then: cat token.json

tasks.explain:
The secret in your config is now exchangeable, and the thing riding on every
request dies in an hour. You also asked for the narrowest scope the control
allows — a leaked users:read token cannot delete users. That narrowing is a
control in its own right.

tasks.instruction:
Pull EVERY page. Call `GET /api/v2/users` with your bearer token and save page 1
as `pulled-page-1.json`. Find `pagination.next_cursor` in it, follow the cursor
(`?cursor=...`) to page 2, save it as `pulled-page-2.json`, and confirm the
cursor came back null — that is the API saying "no more".

hints.nudge: Send the token as `-H 'Authorization: Bearer <your access_token>'`. Page 1's pagination block carries the cursor for page 2; quote the URL when it has a `?` in it.

hints.concept: §4.4 — loop until the API says stop: a null cursor, not your patience, ends the pull

hints.reveal: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token from token.json>' acme.example/api/v2/users > pulled-page-1.json, then grep next_cursor pulled-page-1.json, then: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <same token>' 'acme.example/api/v2/users?cursor=eyJwYWdlIjoyfQ==' > pulled-page-2.json

tasks.explain:
One logical question took two authenticated requests, and only the null cursor
told you that you were done. Both pages advertise total: 8 — you accumulated
5 + 3. The pull is provably complete, which is exactly what the aggregator will
check mechanically in a moment.

tasks.instruction:
Prove 401 and 403 are different facts. Request a SECOND token scoped only
`devices:read` (save it as `devices-token.json`), aim it at `/api/v2/users` with
`-i`, and keep the refusal as `scope-error.txt`. Then point the same token at the
endpoint it IS scoped for — `/api/v2/devices`, saved as `devices.json` — and
count the unencrypted laptops into `unencrypted-count.txt`
(the records carry a `disk_encrypted` field).

hints.nudge: Same token request as t3 with `scope=devices:read`. The 403 means: authenticated fine, not allowed THIS question. Count with `grep -c '"disk_encrypted": false' devices.json`.

hints.concept: §4.2/§4.3 — 401 is authentication, 403 is authorization; least-privilege scopes make the difference visible

hints.reveal: curl -s -d 'grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=grc_evidence_bot&client_secret=cs_4d2b9e7f1a8c6053b4e2d9f7c1a08e35&scope=devices:read' acme.example/oauth/token > devices-token.json · curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token from devices-token.json>' acme.example/api/v2/users > scope-error.txt · curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <same token>' acme.example/api/v2/devices > devices.json · grep -c '"disk_encrypted": false' devices.json > unencrypted-count.txt

tasks.explain:
The devices token authenticated perfectly and was still refused the users
question — that is authorization, not authentication, and your evidence files
now show both refusals side by side. And notice what the devices pull just
computed: one laptop with disk_encrypted false. The same claim you checked on a
single machine in earlier modules ("this laptop's disk is encrypted") just
became a fleet-wide API question.

tasks.instruction:
Now the offline half — the bundled fixtures are byte-identical to what you just
pulled. Open `fixtures/users-page-1.json` and identify the field that holds the
control's truth and the field that says whether more pages exist: grep for each
(`mfa_enabled`, `next_cursor`) so the locations are in your history.

hints.nudge: One boolean per user record answers the control claim; one field in the pagination block answers "did I get everyone?".

hints.concept: §5.1 — LOCATE: the endpoint and field that hold the claim's truth

hints.reveal: cat fixtures/users-page-1.json, then: grep -n mfa_enabled fixtures/users-page-1.json · grep -n next_cursor fixtures/users-page-1.json

tasks.instruction:
Feel the silent-incompleteness trap. Count users without MFA from page 1 alone
into `page1-count.txt`, then recompute over BOTH pages combined into
`combined-count.txt` (compose `cat` and `grep -c` with a pipe). Compare the two
numbers — the API told you in advance they would differ.

hints.nudge: `grep -c '"mfa_enabled": false'` counts matching records. For the combined number, `cat` both pages into one stream first.

hints.concept: §4.4 — a pull that stops early doesn't error; it under-reports, confidently

hints.reveal: grep -c '"mfa_enabled": false' fixtures/users-page-1.json > page1-count.txt, then: cat fixtures/users-page-1.json fixtures/users-page-2.json | grep -c '"mfa_enabled": false' > combined-count.txt

tasks.explain:
Page 1 alone said 2; the complete dataset says 4. No error, no warning — just a
wrong number that looks right. The only advance notice was pagination metadata:
next_cursor was non-null and total was 8 when you'd only seen 5 records.

tasks.instruction:
Run the lab's aggregator over BOTH pages and keep the audit-ready record:
`aggregate-mfa fixtures/users-page-1.json fixtures/users-page-2.json > mfa-report.json`,
then read it. Confirm `total_users` matches the total the pages advertise, and
find the line that explains why the report carries TWO no-MFA numbers — grep the
report for `u_004` and for `active_users_without_mfa`.

hints.nudge: The aggregator takes every page as an argument — give it both. On your own machine this is `bun aggregate-mfa.ts …`; this box runs its byte-locked PATH port.

hints.concept: §5.3 — aggregate across pages, THEN compute; the report surfaces both numbers and lets the control definition decide

hints.reveal: aggregate-mfa fixtures/users-page-1.json fixtures/users-page-2.json > mfa-report.json, then: cat mfa-report.json · grep -n u_004 mfa-report.json · grep -n active_users_without_mfa mfa-report.json

tasks.explain:
total_users is 8 — it matches the advertised total, so the completeness check
passed and this number is trustworthy. The report says users_without_mfa: 4 but
active_users_without_mfa: 3, because u_004 (dave) is suspended. A good evidence
record shows both and hides neither.

tasks.instruction:
Prove the tool refuses to lie. Run the aggregator over ONLY page 1, capturing its
complaint into `incomplete-error.txt` (stderr — remember `2>`), then keep the
exit code as evidence: `echo $? > truncated-exit.txt`. Read the complaint.

verify.regex: incomplete pull: aggregated 5 users but API reported total=8

hints.nudge: stdout and stderr are different channels: `2>` captures the complaint. `$?` still holds the exit code on the very next line you type.

hints.concept: §5.4 — the failure that LOOKS like success, and the completeness check that refuses it

hints.reveal: aggregate-mfa fixtures/users-page-1.json 2> incomplete-error.txt, then: echo $? > truncated-exit.txt · cat incomplete-error.txt

tasks.explain:
Five records, total=8 → the tool refused to emit a report at all and exited 1.
Failing loud beats emitting a smaller number, because a wrong-but-plausible
metric would sail through review and become the control's official truth.

tasks.instruction:
Map the exit codes — the machine-readable verdict. Re-run the full two-page
aggregation and keep its code (`echo $? > exit-fail.txt`). Then build a tiny
all-pass page as `fixtures/users-allpass.json` (one user, `mfa_enabled` true,
total 1, null cursor — same shape as the lab pages), run the aggregator on it as
`allpass-report.json`, and keep that code as `exit-pass.txt`. You already hold
the tooling-error code in `truncated-exit.txt`. Three different numbers, three
different meanings.

hints.nudge: A control FAIL is not a broken tool: a monitoring system must react differently to "the control failed" vs "the check itself broke". One page with every user compliant makes the PASS path observable.

hints.concept: §5.4 — exit-code discipline: 0 control PASS, 3 control FAIL, 1 tooling error

hints.reveal: aggregate-mfa fixtures/users-page-1.json fixtures/users-page-2.json > mfa-report.json · echo $? > exit-fail.txt · echo '{ "data": [ { "id": "u_x", "email": "x@acme.example", "mfa_enabled": true, "status": "active" } ], "pagination": { "page": 1, "per_page": 5, "total": 1, "next_cursor": null } }' > fixtures/users-allpass.json · aggregate-mfa fixtures/users-allpass.json > allpass-report.json · echo $? > exit-pass.txt

tasks.explain:
0 = control PASS, 3 = control FAIL, 1 = tooling error. FAIL and broken-tool MUST
be different codes: a scheduler alerting on "control failed" when the truth is
"the pull broke" pages the wrong team and buries the real defect — module 13
builds its monitoring loop directly on this distinction.

tasks.instruction:
Write the LOCATE plan — the §4.7 five-question docs summary for this vendor —
as `LOCATE-plan.md` next to the fixtures (nano works here, or compose it with a
heredoc). Cover: auth rung + how a token is obtained; endpoint + truth field;
pagination shape + stop signal; rate limit; error shape.

hints.nudge: Everything you need is in vendor-docs.md and in what you just did — five short lines answer it. §5.1 is the worked example of exactly this plan.

hints.concept: §4.7/§5.1 — the five-question plan IS the LOCATE stage; the rest is mechanics

hints.reveal: nano LOCATE-plan.md (or cat > LOCATE-plan.md << 'EOF' … EOF) with one line each — auth: OAuth2 client-credentials at /oauth/token, scope users:read; truth: GET /api/v2/users, field mfa_enabled; pagination: cursor, stop at next_cursor null, total advertised; rate limit: 600 req/min, 429 carries Retry-After; errors: { "error": "...", "message": "..." }

tasks.explain:
That plan is transferable: a GRC engineer who can produce it from cold docs can
pull evidence from a vendor they had never seen an hour earlier. It is also the
document a reviewer audits when they ask "why do you trust this pull?"

tasks.instruction:
Make the evidence provably reproducible. Run the full aggregation twice, into
`report-run-1.json` and `report-run-2.json`, then `diff` the two and record the
verdict: if diff is silent, write `identical` into `repro-verdict.txt` (chain
it: `diff … && echo identical > repro-verdict.txt`).

hints.nudge: `diff a b` prints nothing and exits 0 when the files are byte-identical; `&&` runs the next command only on that success.

hints.concept: §5.3/§6 task 8 — identical evidence on re-run is what makes a pull schedulable; the report pins collected_at for exactly this reason

hints.reveal: aggregate-mfa fixtures/users-page-1.json fixtures/users-page-2.json > report-run-1.json · aggregate-mfa fixtures/users-page-1.json fixtures/users-page-2.json > report-run-2.json · diff report-run-1.json report-run-2.json && echo identical > repro-verdict.txt

tasks.explain:
Byte-identical reports on re-run — the property that turns a one-off pull into a
schedulable control check. On your real machine the §6 step finishes this:
`git init`, commit the fixtures, the aggregator, LOCATE-plan.md, and a README —
then the evidence has history as well as reproducibility.

tasks.instruction:
Explain, to a non-technical colleague, what just happened at the counter — using
§3's service-counter model and tracing ONE of your requests end to end: the verb
and address you asked at, how you proved who you were, what the three-digit
verdict meant, and what shape the answer came back in. Include why your 401 and
your 403 were different sentences in that conversation.

hints.nudge: The §3 model: a deliberate, narrow counter in front of an interior you never touch — verb, address, credential, verdict, JSON answer.

tasks.instruction:
Your report shows users_without_mfa: 4 and active_users_without_mfa: 3 — the gap
is u_004, who is suspended. Citing the control claim ("every workforce user has
MFA enabled"), decide which number you would put in front of an auditor and
defend it in 2–3 sentences. There is a defensible case for each — what matters
is that the scoping decision is explicit, not silent.

hints.nudge: Is a suspended account a "workforce user"? The report deliberately refuses to decide that for you.

hints.concept: §5.3 — the report surfaces both numbers and lets the control definition decide

tasks.instruction:
Two failure modes, one sentence each. First: why is failing LOUD on an incomplete
pull (what you saw in the truncated run) better GRC behavior than emitting a
smaller, plausible number? Second: the vendor docs cap you at 600 requests/minute
and answer excess with 429 + Retry-After — describe what your pull script should
DO when that arrives mid-pagination, and what silently dropping the page would do
to your evidence.

hints.nudge: Both failure modes end the same way if mishandled: a complete-looking report that is quietly missing records.

hints.concept: §4.5 — rate limits and pagination collide: the same pull that needs every page needs to wait politely to finish at all

tasks.instruction:
In one or two sentences, connect "the report is byte-identical on re-run" and
"the whole thing lives in Git" to continuous, audit-ready assurance. (On a real
machine, finish §6 task 8 for real: git init, commit the fixtures, the
aggregator, LOCATE-plan.md, and a short README stating the control and how to
re-run — this box honestly has no git.)

hints.nudge: An auditor's two favorite questions: "can you produce this again?" and "what did it say last quarter?" — which property answers which?

hints.concept: §6 task 8 — version-controlled, reproducible evidence is the bridge to module 13's continuous monitoring

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CI lab-reproduction smoke test for Module 06.
# Asserts the §6 guided lab's CORE LOGIC still reproduces on a clean machine
# (bash + coreutils + bun; NO network, NO cloud creds, NO containers):
#   - the aggregator concatenates the `data` arrays ACROSS BOTH pages (8 users, not 5)
#   - the control metric "users without MFA" is computed correctly (= 4) over the
#     COMPLETE, paginated dataset
#   - the active-only sub-metric is correct (= 3; the suspended no-MFA user is excluded)
#   - the completeness guard fails LOUD when a page is dropped (single-page pull != total)
#   - the exit code is the machine-readable verdict (3 = control FAIL, 0 = PASS)
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL: bun is required for this lab harness"; exit 1; }

# Regenerate the fixtures from clean (proves setup.sh is self-contained).
bash "$HERE/setup.sh" "$WORK/fixtures" >/dev/null
test -f "$WORK/fixtures/users-page-1.json" || { echo "FAIL: setup did not create page 1"; exit 1; }
test -f "$WORK/fixtures/users-page-2.json" || { echo "FAIL: setup did not create page 2"; exit 1; }

# --- Assertion 1: COMPLETE pull over BOTH pages -> control FAIL (exit 3), metric = 4 ---
set +e
REPORT="$(bun "$HERE/aggregate-mfa.ts" "$WORK/fixtures/users-page-1.json" "$WORK/fixtures/users-page-2.json")"
RC=$?
set -e
test "$RC" -eq 3 || { echo "FAIL: expected control-FAIL exit 3, got $RC"; exit 1; }

# Pull scalar fields out of the JSON record with coreutils only (no jq dependency).
field() { printf '%s\n' "$REPORT" | grep "\"$1\"" | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }

TOTAL="$(field total_users)"
NOMFA="$(field users_without_mfa)"
ACTIVE_NOMFA="$(field active_users_without_mfa)"
PAGES="$(field pages_aggregated)"

test "$TOTAL" = "8" || { echo "FAIL: expected 8 aggregated users (both pages), got '$TOTAL'"; exit 1; }
test "$NOMFA" = "4" || { echo "FAIL: expected 4 users without MFA, got '$NOMFA'"; exit 1; }
test "$ACTIVE_NOMFA" = "3" || { echo "FAIL: expected 3 ACTIVE users without MFA, got '$ACTIVE_NOMFA'"; exit 1; }
test "$PAGES" = "2" || { echo "FAIL: expected 2 pages aggregated, got '$PAGES'"; exit 1; }
printf '%s\n' "$REPORT" | grep -q '"control_result": "FAIL"' || { echo "FAIL: control_result should be FAIL"; exit 1; }

# --- Assertion 2: the COMPLETENESS guard catches a truncated pull (page 2 dropped) ---
# If pagination stops early, the answer would be a LIE; the harness must refuse it.
set +e
bun "$HERE/aggregate-mfa.ts" "$WORK/fixtures/users-page-1.json" >/dev/null 2>"$WORK/err.log"
TRUNC_RC=$?
set -e
test "$TRUNC_RC" -eq 1 || { echo "FAIL: truncated pull should error (exit 1), got $TRUNC_RC"; exit 1; }
grep -q "incomplete pull" "$WORK/err.log" || { echo "FAIL: completeness guard did not fire on truncated pull"; exit 1; }

# --- Assertion 3: a PASS scenario returns exit 0 (every user has MFA) ---
mkdir -p "$WORK/all-pass"
cat > "$WORK/all-pass/page-1.json" <<'JSON'
{ "data": [ { "id": "u_x", "email": "x@acme.example", "mfa_enabled": true, "status": "active" } ],
  "pagination": { "page": 1, "per_page": 5, "total": 1, "next_cursor": null } }
JSON
set +e
bun "$HERE/aggregate-mfa.ts" "$WORK/all-pass/page-1.json" >/dev/null 2>&1
PASS_RC=$?
set -e
test "$PASS_RC" -eq 0 || { echo "FAIL: all-MFA dataset should PASS (exit 0), got $PASS_RC"; exit 1; }

echo "PASS: Module 06 lab reproduces (aggregated=$TOTAL across $PAGES pages, no-MFA=$NOMFA, active-no-MFA=$ACTIVE_NOMFA; completeness guard fires; PASS path exits 0)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Module 06 lab fixture generator (original lab asset).
# Usage: setup.sh [DEST_DIR]   (default ./fixtures, alongside this script)
#
# Writes a TWO-PAGE simulated SaaS "list users" API response. The pages model a
# real cursor-paginated endpoint: page 1 carries a non-null next_cursor, page 2
# carries next_cursor=null (the stop signal). Each page advertises the same grand
# total so a completeness check is possible. Eight users; four have mfa_enabled=false
# (one of those is suspended), so the control metric is unambiguous and verifiable.
set -euo pipefail
DEST="${1:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/fixtures}"
mkdir -p "$DEST"

cat > "$DEST/users-page-1.json" <<'JSON'
{
  "data": [
    { "id": "u_001", "email": "alice@acme.example", "mfa_enabled": true,  "status": "active" },
    { "id": "u_002", "email": "bob@acme.example",   "mfa_enabled": false, "status": "active" },
    { "id": "u_003", "email": "carol@acme.example", "mfa_enabled": true,  "status": "active" },
    { "id": "u_004", "email": "dave@acme.example",  "mfa_enabled": false, "status": "suspended" },
    { "id": "u_005", "email": "erin@acme.example",  "mfa_enabled": true,  "status": "active" }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 5,
    "total": 8,
    "next_cursor": "eyJwYWdlIjoyfQ=="
  }
}
JSON

cat > "$DEST/users-page-2.json" <<'JSON'
{
  "data": [
    { "id": "u_006", "email": "frank@acme.example", "mfa_enabled": false, "status": "active" },
    { "id": "u_007", "email": "grace@acme.example", "mfa_enabled": true,  "status": "active" },
    { "id": "u_008", "email": "heidi@acme.example", "mfa_enabled": false, "status": "active" }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 2,
    "per_page": 5,
    "total": 8,
    "next_cursor": null
  }
}
JSON

echo "Module 06 fixture written: $DEST/users-page-1.json, $DEST/users-page-2.json"

# acme.example — API Reference (v2)

> Developer documentation for the Acme workforce platform's REST API. This is the
> document the LOCATE stage reads: every answer your evidence pull needs is on this
> page. (Simulated vendor — this host exists only inside the lab.)

## Authentication

Two rungs are supported. Use the lowest-risk rung your tooling allows, with the
narrowest scope your job needs.

- **API key (legacy):** send `Authorization: Api-Key 9f8c4e21b6a94d3f8c7e5a1029384756`
  on every request. Keys do not expire — prefer OAuth2 below.
- **OAuth2 client-credentials (recommended):** exchange your client credentials for a
  short-lived bearer token at the token endpoint, then send
  `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every API call.

```
POST /oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<id>&client_secret=<secret>&scope=<scope>
```

Lab credentials: `client_id=grc_evidence_bot`,
`client_secret=cs_4d2b9e7f1a8c6053b4e2d9f7c1a08e35`.

Response: `{ "access_token": "...", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "scope": "..." }`.
Tokens live one hour. Requests with no credential answer `401`; a valid token that
lacks the endpoint's scope answers `403`.

### Scopes (least privilege)

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `users:read` | read access to `/api/v2/users` |
| `devices:read` | read access to `/api/v2/devices` |

## Endpoints

### `GET /api/v2/users`

Lists workforce users. Requires scope `users:read`. Each record carries `id`,
`email`, `mfa_enabled` (boolean), and `status` (`active` or `suspended`).

### `GET /api/v2/devices`

Lists managed endpoint devices. Requires scope `devices:read`. Each record carries
`id`, `user_id`, `hostname`, `disk_encrypted` (boolean), and `os`.

## Pagination

List endpoints are cursor-paginated. Every response carries:

```
"pagination": { "page": N, "per_page": 5, "total": T, "next_cursor": "..." }
```

Pass `?cursor=<next_cursor>` to fetch the next page. **Stop when `next_cursor` is
`null`.** Every page advertises the same grand `total` — verify your accumulated
record count against it before trusting any number you compute.

## Rate limits

600 requests per minute per credential. Exceeding the window answers
`429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Wait that long, then
retry the same request — do not drop the page and do not hammer the endpoint.

## Errors

Every non-2xx response body has the shape:

```
{ "error": "<machine-readable code>", "message": "<human-readable explanation>" }
```

Read the status code before the body: `2xx` parse, `401` authenticate, `403` fix the
scope, `404` fix the address, `429` honor `Retry-After`, `5xx` retry with backoff.

tools.aggregate-mfa:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lab tool (module 06 §6 tasks 3-6): the lab box's PATH port of the repo's
# labs/aggregate-mfa.ts core logic. This box has no bun runtime (pinned-container
# negative space), so the aggregator ships as this bash+awk port. The report bytes,
# the completeness guard, and the exit codes (0 control PASS / 3 control FAIL /
# 1 tooling error) are byte-locked to the real `bun aggregate-mfa.ts` output over
# the lab's committed page shape (one user record per line, `"key": value` single-
# space style, as labs/setup.sh writes and the mock vendor serves) — the docker
# capture m06-aggregate-both asserts the equality against a fixture diffed with
# the real tool's output. Re-shaped/arbitrary JSON is outside this port's surface:
# run the real `bun aggregate-mfa.ts` on your own machine for that.

if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: usage: aggregate-mfa <page-1.json> [page-2.json ...]" >&2
  exit 1
fi

for p in "$@"; do
  if ! test -f "$p"; then
    echo "ERROR: could not read or parse JSON page: $p" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if ! grep -q '"data"' "$p"; then
    echo "ERROR: page $p has no 'data' array" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Aggregate ACROSS ALL pages (the .ts concatenates every page's data array).
TOTAL=$(awk '/"id":/ { n++ } END { print n + 0 }' "$@")
HAVETOTAL=$(awk '/"total":/ { h = 1 } END { print h + 0 }' "$@")
EXPECTED=$(awk '/"total":/ { i = index($0, "\"total\":"); t = substr($0, i + 8) + 0 } END { print t + 0 }' "$@")

# COMPLETENESS CHECK (same rule, same message, same exit code as the .ts):
# an evidence pull is only valid if it is COMPLETE. Fail loud, refuse to report.
if [ "$HAVETOTAL" -eq 1 ]; then
  if [ "$TOTAL" -ne "$EXPECTED" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: incomplete pull: aggregated $TOTAL users but API reported total=$EXPECTED (missing pages? truncated pagination?)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

NOMFA=$(awk '/"mfa_enabled": false/ { n++ } END { print n + 0 }' "$@")

# Emit the audit-ready record — byte-identical to JSON.stringify(record, null, 2)
# from the real tool (collected_at pinned for reproducible evidence, as in the .ts).
awk -v npages="$#" '
  /"id":/ { n++ }
  /"mfa_enabled": false/ {
    i = index($0, "\"id\": \"");     r = substr($0, i + 7);  q = index(r, "\""); id = substr(r, 1, q - 1)
    i = index($0, "\"email\": \"");  r = substr($0, i + 10); q = index(r, "\""); em = substr(r, 1, q - 1)
    i = index($0, "\"status\": \""); r = substr($0, i + 11); q = index(r, "\""); st = substr(r, 1, q - 1)
    item = "    {\n      \"id\": \"" id "\",\n      \"email\": \"" em "\",\n      \"status\": \"" st "\"\n    }"
    if (buf == "") buf = item
    else buf = buf ",\n" item
    nomfa++
    if (st == "active") an++
  }
  END {
    nv = n + 0
    mv = nomfa + 0
    av = an + 0
    print "{"
    print "  \"control\": \"MFA enforced for all workforce users\","
    print "  \"framework_ref\": \"SOC 2 CC6.1 / CIS Control 6.5\","
    print "  \"collected_at\": \"2026-05-28T00:00:00Z\","
    print "  \"pages_aggregated\": " npages ","
    print "  \"total_users\": " nv ","
    print "  \"users_without_mfa\": " mv ","
    print "  \"active_users_without_mfa\": " av ","
    if (mv == 0) {
      print "  \"offending_users\": [],"
      print "  \"control_result\": \"PASS\""
    } else {
      print "  \"offending_users\": ["
      print buf
      print "  ],"
      print "  \"control_result\": \"FAIL\""
    }
    print "}"
  }
' "$@"

if [ "$NOMFA" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi
exit 3
